title: Little Worlds: Cozy Reading Nook — FLUX.2 Prompt Laboratory
purpose: Controlled prompt experiment before locking the production visual bible. Every variant depicts the same core reading-nook concept so differences are attributable mainly to prompt structure, length, emphasis, and detail controls.
core_scene: Cozy neighborhood bookstore reading nook with a large armchair, arched window, one bookshelf, small round table with one cup, one potted plant, and one round rug.
success_criteria: Large shapes are enjoyable to color by hand.
Every secondary object has a clear purpose.
Micro-details are limited and large enough for print scale.
Linework is clean and printable with obvious object boundaries.
The visual identity remains coherent across prompt formulations.
One strongest prompt family emerges before scaling to a full book.

pages.label: C1 · long-structured-prose
pages.prompt: Create an original cozy storybook coloring illustration of a tiny neighborhood bookstore reading nook. The primary focus is one large plush armchair positioned in the foreground. Behind it is a single tall arched window with simple curtains. To one side is one rounded wooden bookshelf containing large, clearly separated book shapes. Beside the chair is one small round side table with one simple cup, plus one potted plant and one circular rug. The room should feel complete but intentionally simple. Use crisp black ink on white paper, bold rounded outer contours, lighter but still clean interior lines, medium-large forms, clear separation between objects, and generous uninterrupted areas for coloring. Use an eye-level three-quarter viewpoint and a calm, welcoming composition.

pages.hypothesis: Test 80+ word natural-language prompts to see whether extra specification improves control or instead causes clutter.
pages.label: C2 · long-minimal
pages.prompt: Draw a charming little-world bookstore reading corner with a strong sense of simplicity. The scene contains a comfortable armchair, a single arched window, one bookshelf, one small round side table, one potted plant, and one rug. Give each object enough visual space to be easy to recognize and color. Make the armchair and window the strongest shapes, with the shelf and table supporting them. Render original hand-drawn black line art with rounded forms, smooth confident contours, medium-weight interior details, and large white coloring regions. The final page should feel rich because of composition and silhouette, not because it contains many tiny objects. Use a calm three-quarter interior view.

pages.hypothesis: Test 80+ word natural-language prompts to see whether extra specification improves control or instead causes clutter.
pages.label: C3 · long-purpose
pages.prompt: Create an inviting bookstore reading nook that feels thoughtfully illustrated rather than densely decorated. Place a large rounded armchair slightly forward of center, an arched window behind it, a single tall bookshelf on the left, one tiny round side table on the right, one leafy potted plant near the window, and a simple circular rug beneath the chair. Give the bookshelf a few large book blocks and the table one recognizable cup so every small detail has a clear purpose. Use clean black ink line art, thick friendly contours, rounded storybook geometry, moderate interior detail, large open coloring shapes, and visible foreground, middle ground, and background separation.

pages.hypothesis: Test 80+ word natural-language prompts to see whether extra specification improves control or instead causes clutter.
pages.label: C4 · long-room
pages.prompt: Illustrate a small bookstore room where the reading nook is the only important area. The composition should contain one hero armchair, one arched window, one bookshelf, one side table, one potted plant, and one rug, with simple wall and floor architecture supporting them. Give the chair and window the largest silhouettes and keep everything else secondary. Use original cozy storybook coloring-book aesthetics, black ink contours, clean white interiors, bold smooth outer lines, simpler inner construction lines, and medium-large detail scale. The scene should look polished at full page size and remain comfortable to color by hand.

pages.hypothesis: Test 80+ word natural-language prompts to see whether extra specification improves control or instead causes clutter.
pages.label: C5 · long-expressive
pages.prompt: Create a peaceful bookstore reading corner that communicates warmth through shape and composition. A large rounded armchair sits as the hero object, facing slightly toward the viewer. An arched window frames simple leafy shapes outside. A tall bookshelf sits nearby with a small set of broad book shapes, while a round table holds a single cup. One potted plant and one circular rug complete the scene. Use elegant hand-drawn black ink linework, rounded furniture, strong readable silhouettes, medium-large details, and carefully spaced secondary lines. Make the illustration feel like one coherent world designed by a single illustrator.

pages.hypothesis: Test 80+ word natural-language prompts to see whether extra specification improves control or instead causes clutter.
pages.label: C6 · long-density-test
pages.prompt: Create a cozy bookstore reading nook with the same six purposeful elements: a large armchair, an arched window, one bookshelf, one round side table, one potted plant, and one rug. Explore a moderately detailed coloring-book treatment, but keep the smallest decorative features large enough to remain satisfying at printed page size. Give the bookshelf a handful of large book forms, the table one cup, and the window one simple view beyond it. Use black ink storybook line art, thick rounded outlines, clear object boundaries, restrained decorative motifs, and a balanced three-quarter interior composition.
